office_pockets.entrance: Third Street block, facing the park-side approach

office_pockets.entrance: Clearly signed Market office branch; do not label this block Inner Sunset or Mission

office_pockets.confidence: Occupied historical reporting, consistent later coverage; not a live occupancy guarantee.

office_pockets.district: Central SF office connector — exact district provisional
office_pockets.entrance: Transit branch from Haight, returns to the same stop; district label is a release gate

office_pockets.confidence: SF confirmed; exact district UNVERIFIED. Interior can be assigned now; exterior/map anchor cannot be finalized.

office_pockets.entrance: Signed Fremont office route reached by central transit; return ticket to Japantown/Presidio
office_pockets.anchor: 181 Fremont Street is explicitly named Mercor HQ in company job listings.
office_pockets.confidence: Primary company careers evidence names HQ; exact interior is fictional.

office_pockets.district: Bay Street / North Beach waterfront branch
office_pockets.entrance: Bay Street office pocket north of the main notebook loop
office_pockets.anchor: 295 Bay Street described as Cursor's home in May 2026 local property reporting; legal/mailing address can differ.
office_pockets.confidence: Dated occupied media report plus primary SF-careers confirmation; recheck before final release.

office_pockets.entrance: Separate Sansome/Financial District route, reachable from the North Beach/Chinatown boundary; never relabel it Chinatown

office_pockets.confidence: Listed address, occupancy UNVERIFIED. Keep the route anchor movable until corroborated.

office_pockets.entrance: Howard Street office branch from the downtown transit hub
office_pockets.anchor: 2025 principal-place filing lists 500 Howard; newer reports concern expansion leases. Use the supported corridor, not an unsupported assertion of a particular current door.
office_pockets.confidence: District supported; exact occupied release door remains research-gated.

office_pockets.entrance: Clearly labeled Mission Bay branch north of the Dogpatch workshop route; return transit to Chinatown

office_pockets.confidence: Primary registered-address evidence supports proposed district, not physical occupancy. Verify release-door before final map art.

puzzle: Read the team plan; optional Walden/Steven practice battles teach physical/special/status choices.
Stabilize blue INPUT, then green OUTPUT; wrong order explains and preserves state.
Immediate danger is contained before the leader readiness prompt.
gyms.battle: Small complementary team; Reflect and varied coverage make switching and move categories useful. Preserve the implemented level-6/7/8 draft until an explicit balance revision.
counters: Special attacks that bypass Reflect's physical reduction.
A mixed team with a safe answer to the water/grass/electric coverage.
Status, healing and a deliberately chosen switch rather than repeatedly tackling.
gyms.contribution: Coordinate the independent recovery tasks; certify safe sequencing at a live relay.
gyms.reward: Existing Build Badge and Reflect reward; retain bag-full reward pickup.
gyms.revisit: Scott's incident log acknowledges all eight contributions; rematch tests several plans rather than one combo.

puzzle: Collect three field-note cards, each naming a prerequisite rather than a hidden keyword.
Place observation → isolation → repair in the correct order on a dependency board; wrong placement is undoable.
Route a helper to the visible exit once all dependencies are satisfied; no real account or typing required.
gyms.battle: Three-monster team with clearly separated setup, support and finisher roles. The introductory board previews the dependency, rather than concealing a scripted unwinnable opening.
counters: Pressure the setup role before the finisher benefits.
Use a status or disruption move to break the order.
Build a defensive answer that outlasts finite move/item resources.
gyms.contribution: Order the recovery plan; each later repair gets a clear prerequisite and rollback point.
gyms.reward: Plan Badge; modest supplies and one balanced move-disk slot chosen during balancing. Story itinerary is granted regardless of bag space.
gyms.revisit: Ivan shows the original dependency board next to a tidy but genuinely varied city field log.

puzzle: See two beautiful habitat panels and a live condition marker.
Walk to the corresponding real sample plots; identify three discrepancies using visible clues, not color alone.
Choose the healthy route from independent evidence; a decoy loops back with a short hint.
gyms.battle: Three-monster team demonstrates decoys, accuracy pressure or substitutes using ordinary supported mechanics. No arbitrary invisible target rule; accessibility cues duplicate visual evidence in text.
counters: Reliable accuracy and attacks that answer the demonstrated decoy strategy.
Status or defensive play that reduces pressure while checking the opponent's plan.
A varied team that can take the shown hit and retaliate without relying on a single risky move.
gyms.contribution: Validate that the recovery display matches a live habitat; a convincing picture cannot certify health.
gyms.reward: Lens Badge; optional cosmetic postcard; balanced move-disk slot is contributor proposal, never a progression key.
gyms.revisit: One display intentionally looks ordinary because it now reports an unremarkable real condition.

puzzle: Meet three specialist stations with explicit strengths and limits.
Assign lab-provided helpers to observe, shelter and route tasks; do not demand that the player's party contain particular species.
Test the combined plan; a mismatch explains its consequence and allows reassignment.
gyms.battle: Four-monster team covers complementary offensive and defensive roles. Staff teams foreshadow role changes so winning is not a hidden roster quiz.
counters: Use pivoting and type coverage to prevent a single support role dominating.
Exploit the previewed slow role with a faster ordinary attacker.
Win through defensive sustain and limited-resource management rather than a required rare counter.
gyms.contribution: Assign distinct recovery roles so no one companion is expected to handle every habitat.
gyms.reward: Crew Badge; field-kit supply bundle with deferred claim if bag is full.
gyms.revisit: Brendan's job board finally includes a task whose correct assignment is 'leave this habitat alone'.

puzzle: Observe a visible route fault in a contained simulation; no production habitat is at risk.
Apply one of three reversible patches and run a short test that exposes a side effect.
Restore the last safe state, then apply the minimal correction; display both the success and the rollback path.
gyms.battle: Four-monster team invites adaptation: a telegraphed opening has a second approach. Use ordinary move choices and switches, not a boss that secretly reads the player's selected command.
counters: Prepare a second damage type or attacker when the opening plan is checked.
Use a defensive/status turn to discover the telegraphed pattern safely.
Capitalize on setup turns rather than overcommitting into a predicted switch.
gyms.contribution: Provide a reversible controller update and a way back if the recovery rehearsal fails.
gyms.reward: Patch Badge; balanced recovery/disruption move-disk slot after review.
gyms.revisit: The test suite includes the original bug as a named regression, with an original short joke.

puzzle: Compare three claims: an original observation, a copy of it and a fresh independent measurement.
Follow short source trails to physical markers; duplicated wording is not counted as a second witness.
Open the archive route with two independent observations; all critical clues remain inspectable.
gyms.battle: Four-monster team tests identifying a real pattern without treating one repeated turn as certainty. Preview abilities/roles through trainers; avoid random arbitrary success thresholds.
counters: Check a telegraphed weakness with ordinary type coverage.
Use status or scouting defensively before committing.
Use a complementary second attacker when one plan is visibly countered.
gyms.contribution: Authenticate independent field reports without publishing exact rare-habitat coordinates.
gyms.reward: Source Badge; journal citation stamps are flavor, not a real browsing requirement.
gyms.revisit: Aravind corrects a confidently repeated sentence in the archive and retains the correction.

puzzle: Contain a simulated overload inside a clearly marked boundary.
Set a finite retry budget and a safe stop condition using three readable switches.
Trigger a deliberate test failure, observe safe pause, then recover without erasing earlier work.
gyms.battle: Five-monster defensive team uses finite protection and counterattack options. Differentiate from Dario's late-game specialist by making this gym about knowing when to stop a setup loop.
counters: Taunt/disruption or another supported answer to repetitive setup, if obtainable by this stage.
Special/physical balance or an appropriate wall-breaking move.
Patience, switching and finite-resource pressure with a safe defensive core.
gyms.contribution: Bound retries and protect recovering habitats while the controller changes hands.
gyms.reward: Limit Badge; a modest recovery reward; required rehearsal access never depends on carrying the reward.
gyms.revisit: Daniela's lab visibly keeps a stop switch within reach instead of hiding it behind a puzzle.

puzzle: See four habitat queues and a fixed number of capacity tokens; tokens are lab puzzle objects, not money.
Give each recovering habitat a valid time window; a large queue cannot starve the smaller ones.
Run a schedule under an ordinary temporary capacity drop and recover without inventing infinite resources.
gyms.battle: Five-monster team alternates pressure, support and setup within normal limits. Do not copy Sam's finale identity: this gym tests fair allocation across roles rather than a single scaling ace.
counters: Fast pressure on the exposed role before the next scheduled switch.
Defensive coverage and recovery through the demonstrated rotation.
Disruption of a support role followed by ordinary type advantage.
gyms.contribution: Schedule the eight-part recovery inside available capacity; no unlimited power-up is introduced.
gyms.reward: Flow Badge; final readiness message and balanced move reward with safe deferred pickup.
gyms.revisit: Tibo's wall display leaves capacity unused when the habitats do not need it; the label calls this intentional.
